*[In character as the farmer]*

---

Sixty years I've been working this land. My father farmed it, now it's just me and my wife. The children are all in the city — they send money sometimes, but the farm is ours to manage. Ten mu and a bit. At 72, I move slower than I used to, but I still know what the land needs.

**About my fields:** I put 6 mu in wheat and maize — same ground, wheat in winter, maize in summer, that's how we've always done it here. The other 4 mu and a bit I keep in stevia. The stevia company comes to buy it directly, I don't have to find a market myself. That's why I like it.

---

### Wheat (6 mu) — plant in October, harvest in June

I always plant around Cold Dew festival, early October. I've been planting on the same calendar my whole life and it works. I use seed I saved from last year's harvest — no need to buy when the seed is good. Before planting I hire the tractor to plow and I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. That big white bag from the cooperative, the one with 15-15-15 on it, 50 jin a bag. I scatter it and the tractor mixes it in. Then in spring, around Qingming time, when the wheat is jointing, I walk the rows and look at the color. If it looks yellow and thin I throw some urea on top — maybe 15–20 jin per mu. If the color looks good I might do a little less.

Water is the other thing. I pump from the well four times: once before winter sets in to help the roots, once at jointing in March, once when it's heading in April, and once at grain fill in May if it's dry. Pumping costs money — the electricity runs up — but you can't skip water for wheat. I learned that the hard way in a dry year decades ago.

For pests, I spray a herbicide once in winter when the weeds are small. I hire someone with the equipment to do it, my eyesight isn't good enough for the sprayer anymore. Sometimes aphids come near heading — if the neighbors are spraying I spray too.

Harvest is the combine. Everyone in the village hires the combine now. I watch it go over my 6 mu in two hours. Then I spread the grain on the courtyard to dry.

I expect around 800 jin per mu — maybe 400 kg. Some years more if it rains well in spring, some years less.

---

### Maize (6 mu) — plant in June, harvest in October

Right after the wheat combine leaves, I have to plant maize fast. This is the hardest stretch of the year — hot, tight for time, and my knees hurt. I hire the village tractor service to till and plant in one pass, that costs money but I have no choice. I can't till 6 mu by hand at my age.

For seed I buy hybrid seed from the county supply store — everyone plants hybrid maize now, the old open varieties can't compete. I plant the same variety I planted last year because it did fine. I put down one bag of maize compound fertilizer per mu — the one with more nitrogen — when the tractor plants. Then in August when the plant is tasseling and the ears are forming, I walk the field. If the lower leaves are yellowing I scatter a little urea, maybe 15 jin per mu. If the color is dark I skip it and save the money.

Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat if it rains in summer. I water once at planting to get germination, and once in August if it's dry. The well is shared with two other households so we coordinate.

Harvest in late September, early October — I hire the combine again. My wife and I just pick up the cobs the machine misses.

I expect 800–900 jin per mu for maize. Maybe 420 kg.

---

### Stevia (4.2 mu) — plant in spring, harvest three times before fall

Stevia is different from everything else. You plant seedlings, not seeds — I buy transplants from a neighbor who runs a nursery. I plant in late April or early May when the frost is gone. It's not as demanding as wheat, but the harvesting is all by hand, which is the hard part.

I fertilize stevia light — one small application of compound fertilizer when I plant the seedlings, and a little urea after each cut. Stevia doesn't need as much fertilizer as the grain crops. I water it two or three times over the season — once when transplanting to help it root, once in the dry summer, maybe once more.

We cut the stevia before it flowers — you have to cut before the white flowers open or the leaf quality goes down and the company pays less. I harvest three times: once around July, once in August, once in September. Each time my wife and I cut together. It takes us several days for 4 mu — we're slow now. I sometimes hire one or two young people from the village for a day to help with the big cuts.

The company weighs the fresh leaves and pays me on the spot. I'm not sure exactly how many jin I get — maybe 700–800 jin of fresh leaf per mu for the whole year? It varies.

---

### What worries me this year

Just the labor. Two old people for 10 mu. The wheat and maize I can manage by hiring machines. But stevia harvest, someone has to bend down and cut by hand. My back is not good. If my wife gets sick or I get sick during harvest time, that's a real problem. I try to save a little cash every season just in case I need to hire people on short notice.
